When did I first notice it? Um... well, it's been a while now. I think it's been going on for about a year and eight months. It really started right after my closest friend died. She... she had this beautiful garden. We used to sit out there all the time. She grew these huge sunflowers, the really tall ones that look like they're going to tip over. My friend always told me I was an 'autumn' and should only wear rust or olive green. She was so good at that color season stuff. She had her colors 'done' in the 80s when everyone was doing it. They draped all these fabric swatches over your shoulders in a mall kiosk. Malls are so depressing now, aren't they? Half the stores are closed and the fountains are always turned off. I used to love throwing pennies in the mall fountain when I was little. I wonder what they do with all those pennies when they finally clean it out. Do they donate them? Or just put them in a bank? Pennies cost more to make than they're worth, honestly. They should just get rid of them completely. 

But, um... I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, right, when the problems started. Yeah, it's been about a year and eight months. Ever since she passed away, my brain just hasn't worked the same.

Setting up the carpools for the choir, doing those neighborhood garden plant swaps... oh, and bringing the snacks for the youth basketball games. I used to love doing all that. I'd cut up the orange slices and put them in those little Ziploc bags. Ziploc bags are so bad for the environment, though. I saw this article about microplastics being in everything now, even the rain. Can you imagine? Plastic falling from the sky. It makes me think about those reusable silicone bags, but they're so expensive and they never really get completely dry inside when you wash them. You have to prop them open over a cup or something, and it just takes up so much counter space. My kitchen counters are always cluttered anyway. I have this old toaster oven that I never use, but I can't bring myself to throw it away because it still technically works. It's one of those heavy ones from the 90s. Things were built to last back then. Not like now, where everything is designed to break in a year so you have to buy a new one. Planned obsolescence, they call it. It's a total scam. \n\nBut... yeah, what was I saying? Oh, about the activities. Right. Now... I just don't have the drive for any of it. I can just sit there for hours, staring at my phone, and I don't even feel the push to answer anybody when they text me. It's just... nothing.\n\nDoctor: Since you first noticed the problems, have they steadily gotten worse over time?\n\nPatient: Gotten worse over time? Um... I don't really know if I'd say it's steadily gotten worse. It's just kind of... there. Always there. Like the dust in my apartment. No matter how much I clean, it always comes back. I think it's because I live near the highway. All those cars driving by, kicking up dirt and exhaust. I try to keep the windows closed, but it gets so stuffy, especially in the summer. I bought one of those air purifiers, the ones with the HEPA filters. They say it's supposed to catch 99% of particles, but I'm not sure if it actually works or if it's just a placebo effect. Placebos are fascinating, aren't they? The idea that your brain can trick your body into healing itself just because you think you're taking medicine. I read a study once where they gave people fake knee surgeries—like, they just made the incisions and stitched them back up—and the people actually felt better. Isn't that wild? It really makes you wonder how much of pain is just in our heads. But then again, a broken bone is a broken bone, you know? You can't just think your way out of a cast. My cousin broke his arm falling out of a tree when we were kids. He had to wear this neon green cast for six weeks. Everyone signed it with Sharpies. I drew a little smiley face on the thumb part. I always liked drawing, but I never really pursued it. I thought about taking an art class at the community college, but... I don't know. \n\nBut, uh, the problems getting worse? I'm not sure. I haven't really noticed a steady decline or anything. It's just... the same heavy feeling, day after day.\n\nDoctor: When your mood improves, do your memory and work difficulties improve too, or do they stay the same?\n\nPatient: When my mood improves? Um... I don't know, it doesn't really seem to matter. It's actually the main reason I came in, because my mind just keeps going completely blank at the worst times. Like, I'll be at work—I'm a crossing guard, well, a flagger mostly, for road construction. And I'll just look at the road-closure forms, or even just be holding the stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly cannot remember the steps I've done for years. It's terrifying, honestly, because people's safety is on the line. \n\nCars just drive so fast these days. It's like everyone is in a rush to get somewhere, but where are they even going? Probably just home to sit on the couch. I saw this guy the other day fly through the work zone in a bright red sports car, one of those loud ones that sound like a lawnmower on steroids. Why do people want their cars to be so loud? It just seems obnoxious. It reminds me of my neighbor's son, he plays the drums in his garage every Tuesday and Thursday evening. He's not very good, to be honest. He keeps losing the beat on the cymbals. Cymbals are made of brass, right? Or bronze? I think it's an alloy. My dad used to collect old coins, and he had this special cloth he'd use to polish the copper ones. He kept them in these little plastic sleeves in a big binder. I wonder whatever happened to that binder. Probably sitting in my sister's attic collecting dust. Attics always smell so specific, don't they? Like old paper and dry wood. \n\nBut, um... yeah. The blanking out. It happens whether I'm feeling incredibly down or if I'm having a slightly better day. The confusion is just... it's always there. I just stare at the paddle and my brain is empty.\n\nDoctor: Have people close to you noticed that you repeatedly forget recent conversations or events?\n\nPatient: Have people noticed? Um... no, not really. I mean, nobody's ever said anything to me about forgetting conversations or things that just happened. My sister calls me sometimes, but we usually just talk about her kids. They're both in middle school now. Middle school is such a weird time. I remember when I was in seventh grade, I had this awful haircut. My mom tried to give me a bob, but she cut it way too short in the back, so it looked like a mushroom. I cried for three days straight. I refused to take my school picture that year. I just hid in the bathroom until the photographer packed up. The bathroom smelled like that pink powdered soap, you know the kind? It always left a weird residue on your hands. I hate public bathrooms. The lighting is always so harsh, it makes everyone look sick. Fluorescent lights actually give me a headache if I'm under them for too long. I read somewhere that they flicker at a frequency that can trigger migraines. I wonder if that's true or if it's just one of those internet rumors. There's so much misinformation out there now. You really can't trust anything you read online. \n\nBut, uh, no... nobody has mentioned me forgetting recent stuff. Just the blanking out at work, like I said.\n\nDoctor: Have you had thoughts about dying or killing yourself?\n\nPatient: Thoughts about dying? Um... yeah. I guess I have. It's just... I'm so tired. I really just don't have the energy to fight the thought anymore that maybe it would be better if I just didn't wake up. I actually started saying it out loud recently, which really scares my family. My sister got so upset the other day when I said it. She started crying, and she never cries. Not even when we watched that movie about the dog waiting for its owner at the train station. I bawled my eyes out, but she just sat there. Train stations are kind of depressing anyway, aren't they? All those people coming and going, everyone looking at their phones, nobody really looking at each other. I took a train to Chicago once, years ago. The seats were covered in this scratchy blue fabric, and the person next to me smelled like stale coffee and peppermint. I hate the smell of peppermint. It reminds me of those little hard candies my grandmother used to keep in her purse. They were always covered in lint because they'd fall out of the wrapper. She had this huge leather purse that weighed a ton. I don't know what she kept in there. Probably a brick. \n\nBut, um... yeah. The thoughts about not waking up. It's just... it's exhausting trying to push them away all the time. So I just kind of let them sit there now.\n\nDoctor: Do you have a specific plan to kill yourself?\n\nPatient: A specific plan? Um... no. No plan. I just... like I said, I just don't have the energy to fight the thought anymore that it might be better if I just didn't wake up. I just want to sleep. Sleep is so elusive lately anyway. I bought these new sheets, they're supposed to be Egyptian cotton, but they feel kind of scratchy. I think I got scammed on the internet. You have to be so careful online shopping. My friend bought a sweater once, and when it arrived, it was literally small enough to fit a Barbie doll. She was so mad, but I thought it was hilarious. We used to play with Barbies all the time when we were little. I had the Dreamhouse with the tiny little elevator. The string broke on it, though, so we had to pull it up by hand. I wonder if they still make those. Toys are so electronic now. Everything requires batteries. My sister's kids have these tablets they stare at all day. I worry about their eyes, you know? The blue light. \n\nBut, uh... no. No plan. It just scares my family because I've started saying it out loud, about not wanting to wake up. But I don't have a plan to actually do anything.\n\nDoctor: Have you recently found yourself unsure of what day or date it is?\n\nPatient: Unsure of the day? Um... no, I don't think so. I usually know what day it is. I have to, for work. Being a crossing guard, you really have to stick to the school schedule. Monday through Friday, rain or shine. Sometimes I wish it would just rain all week so I wouldn't have to stand out there, but then the kids get so miserable in the rain. They have these huge backpacks, they look like little turtles struggling to cross the street. I always wonder what they keep in there. Textbooks are so heavy. When I was in college, getting my bachelor's, I had this massive art history book. It must have weighed ten pounds. I had to carry it all the way across campus because the art building was on the complete opposite side from my dorm. My dorm room was so tiny, I shared it with a girl who collected ceramic frogs. She had them everywhere. On the windowsill, on her desk, even on top of the mini-fridge. I knocked one over once and the leg chipped off. I tried to glue it back on, but you could still see the crack. Superglue never really works the way they show it on TV, does it? It just sticks to your fingers and then you're peeling it off for days. \n\nBut, um... no. I know what day it is. I haven't lost track of the date or anything.\n\nDoctor: Do these memory blanks happen in other parts of your daily life, such as managing familiar household tasks, or only while you are working?\n\nPatient: Well, it's... it's happening everywhere, honestly. That's actually why I came in. My mind just keeps going completely blank at the absolute worst times. Like, I'll be at work, and I'll look down at the road-closure forms or I'll be holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just cannot remember the steps. And I've done this for years! It's terrifying. It's like my brain just empties out. \n\nI was trying to make my grandmother's meatloaf the other night—the one with the brown sugar glaze on top. It's the only way meatloaf should be made, really. Ketchup is just too acidic. But I was standing in the kitchen holding the Worcestershire sauce, and I just stared at the bottle for like ten minutes. I couldn't remember if I had already put it in the bowl or if I was supposed to measure it out first. The label on the bottle is so old-fashioned, isn't it? It hasn't changed in decades. I remember my mom having that exact same bottle in the pantry when I was a kid. Our pantry had this squeaky bifold door that would always pinch your fingers if you weren't careful. My brother got his thumb caught in it once and cried for an hour. He was such a crybaby. He still is, honestly. He called me last week complaining about his neighbors playing their TV too loud. Just go over and knock on the door, right? People are so afraid of confrontation these days. \n\nBut yeah... the blanking out. It happens with the meatloaf, it happens with the stop sign at work. I just... I forget everything I'm supposed to do.\n\nDoctor: Have your family members noticed a gradual worsening of your memory or thinking over the past year?\n\nPatient: My family? Um... I don't think so. I haven't really asked them, and they haven't said anything about it being a gradual thing over a year or anything. I don't see them as much as I should, honestly. My sister lives two states over, and we only talk on holidays mostly. She always sends these photo cards for Christmas, you know the ones? Where everyone is wearing matching plaid pajamas and smiling in front of a fireplace. I always wonder if they actually sleep in those or if they just put them on for the picture. Plaid can be so loud. I prefer solid colors for sleeping. I used to have this silk nightgown that was a deep emerald green. It felt so nice, but it had to be dry cleaned. Who dry cleans sleepwear? It's ridiculous. I ended up accidentally washing it in the machine with my towels and it completely ruined it. The fabric got all dull and weirdly stiff. Towels take forever to dry, too. I always have to run my dryer twice to get the bath sheets fully dry. I bought this wool dryer ball that's supposed to speed it up, but it just thumps around in there making a terrible racket. It sounds like someone is throwing shoes around in a metal drum. \n\nBut um, no... my family hasn't said anything about my memory getting worse over the past year. It's just me noticing it lately when it happens.\n\nDoctor: When someone explains a new task to you and you practice it, can you remember how to do it later that same day?\n\nPatient: Um... a new task? I guess I haven't really had to learn anything new lately. I've been doing the same crossing guard route for a while now. But if I did... I don't know, maybe? I feel like if I practiced it, I'd probably remember it. I used to be really good at picking things up quickly. Like when I first learned how to knit. My aunt taught me. She made these incredible afghans, just massive blankets with all these intricate cable patterns. She tried to teach me the cable stitch, but I could never get the tension right. My stitches were always way too tight, so the whole thing would pucker up and look like a little accordion. I ended up just sticking to the basic garter stitch and making scarves. So many scarves. Everyone in my family got a scarf for Christmas that year. I used this really chunky, mustard-yellow yarn. Yellow is such a tricky color to wear, isn't it? It completely washes me out. I look much better in cool tones, like blues and purples. I bought this violet cardigan last week, actually. It has these beautiful pearl buttons down the front. But the buttonholes are a little too small, so you really have to wrestle with them to get it fastened. It's almost not worth the effort to wear it, which is a shame because the color is just gorgeous. \n\nBut, uh, anyway... I'm not really sure about learning new tasks. I haven't tried to learn anything new in a while, so I couldn't say for sure."
